title: The tortoise under the mountain
hook: the mountain starts to sink, and a tortoise dives under it
carry: vishnu sustains: he holds the world from below
tomorrow: they churn for nectar. so why does poison come up first?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Matsya brought the stolen Vedas home: the Vedas are heard, and handed on by mouth. Now the gods need a mountain to churn the sea. Who holds it up?

Tug-of-war at a school field day: two teams, one rope, everyone straining, and then the ground under the middle starts to give. Now make it enormous. A mountain, set point-down into the sea for a churning stick. A great serpent wound around it for a rope. The gods hauling one end, the asuras the other, back and forth, the way a churn turns milk to butter. It's working. And then the mountain begins to sink.
screen: `ONE ROPE, TWO TEAMS.` → `A MOUNTAIN FOR A CHURNING STICK.` → `THE MOUNTAIN SINKS.`

segments.voice: This is the churning of the ocean of milk. In the Vishnu Purana, the gods have lost their strength after a sage's curse, and Vishnu tells them how to win it back: churn the ocean for amrita, the nectar of immortality. They can't do it alone, so they work with the asuras, their rivals, and promise them a share. The mountain is Mandara; the rope is the serpent Vasuki. But a mountain has no floor to stand on in the middle of the sea. So Vishnu comes down a second time, now as a vast tortoise, Kurma. He dives under the mountain and takes it on his back, and the churning goes on, turning on his shell. Here's the teaching inside the picture. Many Hindus learn the one God's work in three faces: Brahma creates, Vishnu sustains, Shiva dissolves. Vishnu's work is keeping the world going, and Kurma is that work with nothing added. He doesn't pull the rope or fight anyone. He holds. That's why so many Hindus pray to Vishnu as the protector, the one who keeps a life standing. And look who's on the rope above him: gods and asuras both. He holds it up for all of them.
screen: `THE OCEAN OF MILK.` · `GODS AND ASURAS ON ONE ROPE.` · `BRAHMA CREATES. VISHNU SUSTAINS. SHIVA DISSOLVES.` · then, large: `KURMA HOLDS THE WORLD UP.`

segments.voice: Sit so your back is supported, by a chair, a wall or the floor. Let it take your whole weight, the way the tortoise takes the mountain, and notice each place where you're held. If you pray, you can rest your weight in Vishnu, the one who sustains; if you don't, just let the floor do the holding.
Kurma: the tortoise, Vishnu's second descent, who holds the mountain while the sea is churned.
Your line: Vishnu sustains: he holds the world from below. Kurma is that, with nothing added. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindus honor Vishnu as the sustainer of the world and Kurma as his second descent; the churning of the ocean is retold from the Puranas and shown in temple carvings, with the tortoise beneath the mountain.
